title: Coroner calls for inquest in death of suspected burglar
subtitle: Ontario's deputy chief coroner has called for an inquest in the 2011 death of a Hamilton man after an altercation with police.
article: Ontario's deputy chief coroner has called for an inquest in the 2011 death of a Hamilton man after an altercation with police.
James Kiteley, 36, died in hospital February 14.
Under the Coroner's Act, an inquest is mandatory.
Kiteley, a suspected burglar, was found by police outside a home on Brighton Avenue.
Responding to an entry-in-progress call at 8 p.m., officers arrived to find two civilians holding Kiteley on the ground.
The Special Investigation Unit was called in after Kiteley was injured during the arrest. His injuries were not known.
Longtime girlfriend Crystal Maloney says his autopsy report revealed Kiteley died of asphyxiation due to compression of the torso.
"Which basically means he was strangled," says Maloney, a nurse of five years at St. Peter's hospital.
"There was no justice for James," she adds. "Paul Bernardo did a lot worse than he ever did, and he's still alive."
Kiteley's family has been open about his lengthy wrap sheet. Maloney says since his teens, he had 'tons' of trouble with the law.
She believes her boyfriend broke into the east end home that day. Detectives told her he stole a television and was caught by the occupants who had returned home.
"I understand what he did wasn't right. You shouldn't steal from people," she says. "But you can't take the law into your own hands."
Aimed at preventing similar deaths, the inquest is expected to last for three days starting Feb. 11 at 9:30 a.m., at the John Sopinka Court House in Hamilton.
The inquest coroner, Jack Stanborough will hear from seven witnesses. David King has been assigned as counsel to the coroner.
